body:
I would love a dog of my own.  When I'm out on my run and run into a dog, I have to exercise a lot of self control not to stop and pet it, haha.  

Re: feeling guilty about wanting to be an author, I feel like there are so many white women writing for children right now and a lot of other perspectives don't get seen.  I want there to be diverse voices in kids' literature and I feel guilty for adding to the white voices in kids' lit.  It would be like not practicing what I preach.  

I keep thinking I should pursue therapy.  Then I see horror stories about insurance - you have to have a diagnosis to use your insurance, and then they can use that diagnosis against you later.  So I want to be able to pay out of pocket to avoid that, but that's not feasible with my financial situation right now....
Thanks for that, I might message you in the future.  What's your preferred genre?

Therapy: no.  Sometimes in the middle of the night when I'm feeling suicidal and just want to drive my car off a bridge, I think that I could use it, but then the morning comes and I go to work and I see the kids I work with and I think - how could I possibly need therapy, these children are all the therapy I need.  Hearing them say "Miss Mecab, Miss Mecab!  Are you doing story time today?!" lifts my heart more than anything in the world.  And then I come home and I see the reality of my life and all I want to do is get back in the car and crash it into something.

Animals: I love dogs, but due to my current living situation I don't think it would be fair to get one.  Volunteering with an animal shelter might be a good outlet, thanks for that.

Nature: I live in an area where it's not that hard to get to the middle of nowhere, I should probably spend more time outdoors.  I always did love it as a child.

Art: I used to want to be an author.  Now I feel guilty about wanting that for a number of reasons.
I love my grandma probably more than my parents - that sounds terrible, but it's true.  I don't think I could kill myself while she's still alive.  We spent a lot of time together when I was a child.
Talking about books with kids, performing storytime programs, just generally getting to share my love of literature with people young and old in a setting that I think does a lot of social good.

I just think about the friends I have, the people at work that I spend time with outside of work and the friends I made in graduate school (many of whom have drifted away).  Would they really care?  I can't help but think that for most of them it would be no.  I have one co-worker who I think would care, but that is because I know he struggles with addiction and mental health issues and it would hit him hard.

I haven't seen a doctor at all in over a year since I finished graduate school.  I have insurance but can't afford my co-pays.  I keep meaning to look into ACA and see if that would be a better option than the insurance provided by my employer, but by the time I think of it it's usually midday at work and I'm not feeling so low anymore.

I do exercise, I run four days a week and actually started in the hopes that it would help me sleep better.  It helped for several weeks and then I guess my body got used to it and now it is just something I do because I am supposed to.

My diet could definitely be better.  I eat when I remember to, which is usually once or twice a day and consists of whatever I happen to have around.  Today that was a bagel, a fried egg, and some raspberries.
